svg.title: Azure Service Availability architecture
svg.desc: GitHub Pages dashboard in the browser; optional Microsoft Entra ID sign-in; API and collector Function apps (Flex Consumption, Indonesia Central) with user-assigned managed identities; VNet integration and private endpoints to Azure Managed Redis and Storage; the collector calls Azure Resource Manager and the Azure Retail Prices API every 6 hours.
svg.text: All outbound traffic from both apps leaves through this subnet
internet egress is platform-managed here · a NAT gateway gives a fixed IP
No secrets in the page or the repo
Managed identities for ARM, Redis, storage
Redis and storage: no public access, no keys

g.text: sign-in (OAuth 2.0 + PKCE) · access tokens · signing keys (JWKS)
issues tokens to the two managed identities
The timer trigger 0 0 */6 * * * runs at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 UTC (07, 13, 19 and 01 WIB). Flex Consumption on Linux always uses UTC for schedules.
Sign in as the managed identity
az login --identity --client-id gets an Azure Resource Manager token for id-asa-collector, which has Reader on the subscription and nothing else.
az account list-locations, az provider list and az rest on Microsoft.Web/geoRegions. Like every outbound call from a Flex Consumption app, it leaves through snet-functions.
az rest GET Microsoft.Compute/skus?$filter=location eq '<region>' for 65 regions, 8 at a time: about 5 s per region instead of about 2 min with az vm list-skus. Restrictions flag sizes that are
The Azure Retail Prices API, filtered to Azure Managed Redis, needs no sign-in and returns up to 1,000 items per page; the collector follows NextPageLink.
az account get-access-token --resource https://redis.azure.com. The cache accepts Microsoft Entra tokens only (access keys are disabled); the username is the identity's object ID.
Through VNet integration to the Redis private endpoint (privatelink.redis.azure.net, TLS port 10000). One MULTI/EXEC transaction writes the gzip JSON documents, the change log and the run record.
'Collection finished' (65 regions, 67,469 VM rows, 0 errors on 18 Nov 2026) goes to Application Insights with Microsoft Entra authentication; local authentication is disabled.
The browser loads the static site from GitHub Pages: HTML, JavaScript and config.js, which holds public IDs only. There are no secrets in the page or the repo.
Call the API without a token
GET /api/summary on func-asa-api-cangze with no Authorization header. CORS on the Function app allows https://ibranibeny.github.io only.
No token means a read-only guest: 120 requests a minute per address and no collector error details. A request with a bad token is refused, never treated as a guest.
The API's own managed identity (id-asa-api) gets a Microsoft Entra token for https://redis.azure.com and reuses it until shortly before it expires.
Out through VNet integration to the Redis private endpoint: GET {asa}:v1:summary (gzip JSON). The app keeps it for 60 seconds.
The API returns the compressed JSON and the map, service matrix, VM finder and Managed Redis views render in the browser.
Authorization code flow with PKCE against the contoso.day tenant (domain_hint=contoso.day). PKCE is required for single-page apps; no secret lives in the page.
The SPA redirect URI lets the browser call the token endpoint (CORS). It returns an access token for Availability.Read; refresh tokens for SPAs last 24 hours.
Call the API with the token
GET /api/summary with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, from the allowed origin https://ibranibeny.github.io.
Signature against the tenant's signing keys (jwks_uri, cached 6 h), then issuer, audience, tenant, the Availability.Read scope, the calling app (azp) and a contoso.day member account.
The API's managed identity gets a token for Redis; the user's token is never passed on to Azure resources.
Same private path as guests: VNet integration, private endpoint, TLS port 10000.
The JSON goes back to the browser, including the collector's run details that guests don't see.
scripts/entra-apps.sh creates or updates the dashboard app (SPA redirect URIs) and the API app (scope Availability.Read) through Microsoft Graph.
az deployment group create runs infra/main.bicep: VNet, subnets, private endpoints and DNS zones, Managed Redis, storage, identities, roles and both Flex Consumption apps, created one after the other
az functionapp deployment source config-zip uploads each app as a Flex Consumption package deployment: the collector (52 MB, with the Azure CLI) and the API (7 MB).
Packages sit in each app's blob deployment container. The apps reach it, and their host storage, through the storage private endpoints with their managed identity; shared keys are off.
A commit to main /docs publishes the site with GitHub Pages (deploy from a branch).
scripts/run-collector.sh calls the collector's admin endpoint to run the timer function once; after that the schedule takes over.
